subject: Enclave boundary evidence request — operator roster + CAIQ/SOC2 packet
messages:
From: Alice Turner <alice.turner@medisys.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Cc: security@medisys.com
Date: Wed, 27 May 2026 09:15:00 +0100
Subject: Request: operator matrix + CAIQ follow-up for EU-only private deployment

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the call this morning. As we discussed, Medisys needs a concise evidence packet to validate that the private deployment bound for our EU tenancy is segregated and staffed in a way that meets our regulator expectations. Specifically we need: 

- A short operator roster (names, roles, limited access windows) showing who has keystore/privatelink/operator access for the EU enclave.
- The latest SOC 2 Type II report and any relevant carve-outs (redacted where necessary).
- CAIQ responses that show network boundary controls, operator access controls, and KMS partitioning/rotation frequency.
- A VPC/privatelink diagram showing peering, egress filters, and where audit logging is collected.

Can you provide a one‑package deliverable (PDF/zip preferred) and an expected delivery date? We need this for our internal audit team and to move the procurement review forward.

Also, a quick confirmation: will operator sessions be restricted to specific bastion jump hosts in the EU region, or do you permit any cross-region operator fallback? That was a key gating item for our legal team.

Appreciate it — if you prefer, we can route the doc via DocuSign so the security lead can acknowledge receipt.

Regards,
Alice Turner
Head of Security Compliance
Medisys Health

From: soojin_lee@redwood.ai

Date: Wed, 27 May 2026 11:04:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Request: operator matrix + CAIQ follow-up for EU-only private deployment

Alice —

Thanks for the clear ask. We're assembling a compliance packet for Medisys that will include the items you listed. Quick clarifications so we deliver exactly what you need: 

1) Operator roster format: we can supply a CSV (name | role | jurisdiction | access scope | typical session window) + a short narrative describing escalation-only cross-region access. Is that acceptable?

2) KMS partitioning: we will include a keystore operator assertion (who has access, separation by key ring per tenant, rotation cadence). Note that HSM-backed keys for EU tenancy are provisioned in the EU region only.

3) SOC2: we will provide the full Type II PDF and an executive summary highlighting controls relevant to private deployments. We will redact employee PII where required.

4) Delivery: target end of day Friday (2026-05-29) for the full packet. If you need something earlier for procurement, we can push an interim set (roster + VPC diagram) by EOD tomorrow.

I'll coordinate with Irene for operator roster and Ben for the VPC diagram and CAIQ mapping.

Action items: 
- Irene to draft operator roster CSV and keystore assertion.
- Ben to export VPC diagram and CAIQ workbook subset.
- Soojin to assemble SOC2 PDF and sign-off package + upload link.

If that timeline works, I'll send the DocuSign wrapper for receipt acknowledgment.

Thanks,
Soojin Lee
Senior Security Solutions
Redwood Inference

From: irene_choi@redwood.ai
To: soojin_lee@redwood.ai, Alice Turner <alice.turner@medisys.com>

Date: Thu, 28 May 2026 14:22:00 -0400
Subject: Operator roster + CAIQ workbook (preliminary)

Hi team,

Attaching the preliminary artifacts for Medisys: operator-roster.csv (redacted employee IDs), CAIQ-Medisys-Response.xlsx, and vpc-diagram-eu-privatelink.png. Notes: 

- operator-roster.csv: lists operators who have explicit keystore or privatelink config rights for the EU enclave. Columns: name, role, jurisdiction, access_scope, approved_hours_utc. Hours are typical maintenance windows; emergency access is logged and requires two‑party approval.
- CAIQ workbook: answers focused on network segregation (AC-PE), operator logging, and KMS practices. There are comments in the workbook where we recommend follow-ups.
- VPC diagram: shows EU-only bastion hosts, dedicated peering to Medisys VPC, and egress firewall placements.

One important callout on cross-region operator fallback: we allow temporary cross-region operator access only under a documented change control (two approvers from our CSIRT + the regional infra lead) and with session recording enabled. That should meet the requirement that keys remain regionally partitioned by default.

Attestations included as separate text file: keystore-operator-assertion.txt (signed by me).

Let me know if you want the roster in a different schema. If Medisys legal wants raw employee IDs removed entirely from our CSV, we can swap to hashed identifiers.

Thanks,
Irene Choi
Director, Cloud Security
Redwood Inference

Soojin / Irene / Ben —

Received the packet, thanks for the quick turnaround. A couple of follow-ups from our audit: 

- Confirm the KMS rotation window for tenant keys (statement in keystore-operator-assertion.txt references quarterly rotation — please confirm whether that is automated or manual).
- For the operator roster CSV, please provide the exact escalation step that allows cross-region access (who signs off, and where the approval record is stored).
